site.title: Applied AI Engineering
site.tagline: Past the taxonomy. Into the argument.
site.description: The flagship synthesis hub — where patterns surfacing across production-ai-patterns, agentic-engineering, scaling-ai-systems, ai-ops-field-notes, fde-field-notes, the-ai-runbook, and awesome-ai-architecture add up to a strategic argument, not just another failure list.

articles.title: The Failure Taxonomy Industrial Complex
articles.hook: Every AI engineering blog in 2026 has published its own list of seven ways agents fail. They agree with each other almost perfectly. That agreement should worry you more than any individual failure.

articles.title: Why Your AI Failure Taxonomy Isn't a Strategy
articles.hook: Every team has a list of ways agents break. Almost none have turned that list into an argument about where to invest next quarter.

articles.title: The Pattern That Keeps Showing Up: Read-Heavy, Write-Cautious
articles.hook: Across seven field-notes repos, the production systems that survived contact with real users share one design instinct — and it isn't the one vendors sell you.

articles.title: What FDEs Know That Platform Teams Don't (Yet)
articles.hook: Forward-deployed engineers absorb chaos that never reaches a postmortem. Their tacit rules are quietly becoming the platform team's next roadmap.

articles.title: On-Call for Agents: Runbooks Are Not Enough
articles.hook: A runbook tells a human what to do when things break. It says nothing about what to do when the thing breaking is itself making decisions.

articles.title: Scaling Laws Are Not Operating Laws
articles.hook: The industry keeps borrowing model-scaling intuition to justify org-scaling decisions. The two curves don't share an X-axis.

articles.title: The Architecture Reference Nobody Finishes Reading — And Why That's Fine
articles.hook: Awesome-lists get bookmarked, not read cover to cover. The value was never completeness; it was the two links you needed at 11pm.
